Same class as #6805/#6806/#6829 — fold into that family's next catalog-fixture round, or batch with other one-line fixture fixes; a dedicated dispatch for one JSON key is overhead. The scope note matters for the family: #6810 exhausted only the `content` key class, and this card is the datum that the non-`content` class is non-empty.

## ⚠️ Why this is being dispatched standalone, when the standing disposition said not to

The triage directive (2026-08-31, `zhuangjianguo`) graded this **p3 · fold-preferred**:

> Same class as #6805/#6806/#6829 — fold into that family's next catalog-fixture round, **or batch with other one-line fixture fixes**; a dedicated dispatch for one JSON key is overhead.

and the predecessor seat recorded it as *"not going out as its own unit"*, held for that fold.

**The fold window has since closed.** #6318 ran exactly the catalog-fixture round this card was waiting for — its dev fixed three fixtures in this same corpus (a `select` label typo, a `button-group` missing label, `tabs` missing `value`) and PR #6944 merged earlier today **without this card folded in**. There is no other one-line fixture fix currently queued to batch it with. Holding it further means holding it for a round that has already gone past.

⇒ Dispatching it as its own unit, at the cheapest tier the risk allows. ⛔ Recording this rather than silently re-picking it from the title — the predecessor's note explicitly asked that a later rotation not do that.

## ZONE 1 — RULING (⛔ not re-adjudicable)

**The repair**, already adjudicated on the card:

> Author the key the renderer reads: `{ "label": "Option 3", "value": "3" }`

**The wrong fix, ruled out — ⛔ do not do this:**

> ⛔ Not "teach `ui:select` to read `type`" — `type` is the node-type key of the JSON protocol and must not acquire a second meaning on option objects (AGENTS.md #0.1).

⇒ Your entire scope is the fixture. ⛔ Do not touch `packages/components/src/renderers/form/select.tsx`, ⛔ do not touch `SelectOption` in `packages/types`. If you find yourself editing a renderer or a type, you have left the fence — stop and report.

## ZONE 2 — PM MECHANISM ASSUMPTIONS (⚠️ unverified by me)

- The card says the third option in `basic-select.json` authors its display text under `type`, and that the renderer reads only `value` / `disabled` / `label` (`select.tsx:61-62`), with `matchOptionValue` reading only `value` (`option-value.ts:38`). **All line numbers are days old — re-derive from the tree.**
- The card says `SelectOption` (`packages/types/src/form.ts:266`) declares `label` required and does not declare `type`, so the fixture is off-contract as well as unrendered.
- ⚠️ **Check first whether this is already fixed.** #6944 landed fixes to fixtures in this exact corpus today, including a `select` label typo. If that was this one, the delivery is `premise_still_valid: false` with evidence — a with-evidence no-op, ⛔ not a manufactured diff.

## The check that the edit was right

Borrow #6318's own test, which triage set for this corpus: **a fixture that does not start rendering differently after "correction" is the sign the edit was wrong.** Before: the third item renders as a select row with no visible text. After: it renders `Option 3`. Show that as a reading, through the real renderer, not as an assertion.

## Premise-first

Read the card's body and both comments on GitHub yourself; check the body for sanitizer truncation and say that you checked. `premise_still_valid: false` is a legitimate delivery.

Leave your own claim comment with your own session ID and branch; ⛔ do not touch the assignee field.

os-dev-report — correction to two sanitizer-eaten fragments

I read my own report comment back to its tail. It survives complete through the closing footer, and its first line is the literal `os-dev-report` marker, so it is machine-visible. But the GitHub body sanitizer consumed two tag-shaped fragments inside it — including one that was load-bearing evidence. Restating both here in placeholder spelling, with no angle brackets.

**1. The `select.tsx:61-62` quote (load-bearing — this is the whole re-derivation).** As posted it reads only as `{opt.label}`, because the JSX element around it was eaten. What line 62 actually says, angle brackets spelled out as words:

- line 61: `{schema.options?.map((opt) => (`
- line 62: OPEN-TAG `SelectItem key={String(opt.value)} value={String(opt.value)} disabled={opt.disabled}` CLOSE-BRACKET then `{opt.label}` then the matching closing `SelectItem` tag.

The point that survives: the element consumes exactly three keys off an option — `value`, `disabled`, `label` — and its only child is `{opt.label}`. There is no fallback from `label` to `value`, which is why an option lacking `label` paints an empty row rather than showing its value.

**2. The `no_mutation` git command.** As posted it reads `git show 29754cf^:` with the path missing. The command actually run was `git show` of the commit-parent revision `29754cf^`, colon, then the fixture path `examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/components-form-select/basic-select.json`.

**3. Stale count in the report.** Its `mcp_calls` field says 4, which was true when written. The true total for this run is **6**: `issue_read(get)`, `issue_read(get_comments)`, the claim comment, the report comment, one paginated `issue_read(get_comments)` to read the report back, and this correction.

Nothing else in the report was altered — the readings, hashes, exit codes and verdict lines all came back byte-intact, since none of them contain a tag shape.

## ACCEPT — `premise_still_valid: false`, no diff, and that is the correct delivery. Closing as already fixed by PR #6944.

`domain:ui` seat, session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`. Reviewed against `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report's self-description.

### ⛔ First: my dispatch order asserted something false, and the dev is the reason it did not become a wasted diff

I wrote, in the claim comment above:

> The fold window has since closed. #6318 ran exactly the catalog-fixture round this card was waiting for … and PR #6944 merged earlier today **without this card folded in**.

**That last clause is wrong.** #6944 *did* fix this exact fixture — commit `29754cf`, a one-line rename of the third option's key from `type` to `label`, byte-for-byte the repair ruled on this card. The "select label typo" I saw in #6944's report and flagged as *possibly* this one **was** this one.

⇒ I inferred the fold had not happened from #6944's summary rather than reading the fixture, then wrote the inference into an order as a fact. ⭐ The only thing that stopped it costing a diff is that the same order's ZONE 2 told the dev to read the file first and treat a spent premise as a complete delivery. **A card reference — including a merged sibling PR — gets re-read, not relayed.** Same failure class this lane recorded on #3880 in August; recorded again because I repeated it.

### Verified independently before writing this

| claim | my reading on `origin/main` |
|---|---|
| the fixture is already repaired | ✅ third option reads `{ "label": "Option 3", "value": "3" }` |
| `29754cf` is in `main` | ✅ `git merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 0 |
| the regression is pinned | ✅ `examples/schema-catalog/test/safe-validate-corpus-6318.test.ts:98` asserts the three labels equal `['Option 1','Option 2','Option 3']` (report cited `:93`; the assertion is at `:98` — immaterial drift, and the pin is real) |
| control: pin file exists | ✅ |

### ⭐ The method that earns the ACCEPT: a before/after render reading with **no mutation**

The check triage set for this corpus is *a fixture that does not start rendering differently after correction is a sign the edit was wrong*. Demonstrating that normally means mutating the tree and restoring it. This run did not:

> the pre-fix document was extracted as a git **blob** from `29754cf^` into a probe-only file; `git hash-object` = `652a086`, identical to the pre-image index in the commit's own diff

⇒ **BEFORE** `["Option 1", "Option 2", ""]` — one blank row. **AFTER** `["Option 1", "Option 2", "Option 3"]`. Both read through the real `SchemaRenderer` in one run. There was no ablation to restore and no window in which the fixture on disk was wrong. ⭐ That is strictly better than mutate-and-restore, and it is the shape to reuse whenever the "before" state exists in history.

⭐ It also produced a **correction to #6944's own commit message**, which describes the fixture as *"the open list showed two options, now three"*. Measured: there were **three** `role=option` elements both before and after; the third one's `textContent` was empty. One blank row, not a missing row. Small, and exactly the kind of thing that becomes a false premise for someone later.

### Housekeeping

- **No changeset owed** — named by the gate (`check-changeset-presence.mjs` exit 0, *"no changeset is owed"*), not by judgement. `examples/schema-catalog` is `private: true` besides.
- **Branch not pushed** — declared, and I agree: with no commit to carry, a remote branch zero commits ahead of `main` reads as abandoned work. ⛔ Not scored as a protocol miss.
- The vitest guard (#3378) rejecting the package-directory launch was reported rather than hidden. That is the documented false-green trap, not a red test.

### Disposition

Closing **completed** — the defect is fixed on `main` and pinned against return. `pm:dispatched` removed and assignee cleared in the same action. ⛔ Nothing here needs a new card.
